Summary Description: Dr. Patrick J. McCann is an interdisciplinary researcher at the University of Oklahoma whose work bridges mid-infrared photonics and thermophotovoltaic (TPV) energy conversion. He co-develops compact mid-IR laser-based sensors for metabolic readouts in hydrogel-based cell cultures and leads analytic TPV device design and modeling using IV–VI MQW materials on silicon. His research demonstrates a blend of experimental sensing platforms (including inline acetaldehyde headspace measurements and lock-in spectroscopy) with advanced materials design and device-level calculations, targeting applications from cancer metabolism sensing to grid-scale, low-cost TPV power generation. The work collectively advances both sensing technology for bioprocess monitoring and scalable, silicon-compatible TPV architectures for energy storage and conversion, highlighting practical pathways toward manufacturability and real-world deployment.
